speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a newborn presenting with feeding intolerance and bilious vomiting. How old is the baby in days, and has the baby passed any meconium stool yet?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, 3050-g (6-lb 12-oz) male, six hours post delivery. The newborn has had several episodes of bilious vomiting and is intolerant to feeding since birth. Was born at term following an uncomplicated pregnancy, though the mother missed several prenatal checkups. The patient's older brother underwent surgery for pyloric stenosis as an infant.

speaker: Doctor
text: The baby is only six hours old and has not passed meconium, which is a significant concern for distal obstruction. I need to see the abdominal imaging to assess for dilated bowel loops or a double bubble sign. REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Bilious vomiting. I also have Feeding intolerance, No fever, Vomiting started within first day after birth.

speaker: Doctor
text: The abdominal X-ray shows a "double bubble" sign with no distal gas, which is classic for duodenal atresia. DIAGNOSIS READY: Duodenal atresia
